title: The way I could’ve easily watched another 3 hours of this play, it is...
transcript: This is one of my favorite new plays that I've seen in a while. It's called birthright, It just opened at MCC Theatre this week. And just to rip the Band Aid off, yes, it is three hours long. but with two intermissions, it really does fly by and I was locked in from start to finish. Birthright explores the evolving friendship of six Jews who met on a birthright trip to Israel. If you don't know what a birthright trip is, it is essentially a free trip that is offered to all Jewish people. So you have these groups of American Jews, usually around college age, being flown out to Israel, getting really drunk and being exposed to a very curated version of Israel. To put it bluntly, it is essentially state propaganda disguised as a free vacation. And so we check in with this group of friends almost immediately after they get back from their trip. Second act is 10 years later, and the third act is eight years after that. And as time goes on, we see their views on Israel start to diverge, especially after the October 7th attacks and all that followed. However, while the debate around Israel Palestine is a big part of this show, it's not really the central focus, nor does it have any interest in picking a side, so to speak. The focus is instead on friendship and found family. and how slash if these relationships can survive, if life takes you in very different directions. The script is by Jonathan Spector, who also wrote Eureka Day. It is so funny and thoughtful and smart. In the way that he'll plant little seeds in the earlier acts that then have pay offs later on. It's brilliant. And a really strong ensemble of actors as well. Some great performances across the board, really bringing out the depth and humanity of these characters. You absolutely understand where all of them are coming from, even the ones you don't agree with. Now, one word of warning that I would give is that this play is very Jewish. They will just drop a lot of Jewish phrases and concepts, and they don't really stop to explain them. And while I do think a lot of it can be gleaned through context clues, If you're not Jewish, I do think that there will be some moments where you're not quite sure what they're talking about. I do think you'll still enjoy the play, but just something to be aware of going in, And maybe bring a Jewish friend to explain some things to you during the intermissions. But Jewish or not, this is definitely a Broadway Ben must see.
classificationReason: First-hand review of Birthright at MCC Theatre. Creator describes the production in detail (three acts, two intermissions, subject matter), clearly attended, and gives a strong positive opinion ('one of my favorite new plays that I've seen in a while').
